title: 2027 Integra Type S Heritage Edition Pays Tribute to the DC2 Type R

body_markdown:
My, how time flies. It’s been 30 years since the[Integra Type R](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/acuras-integra-type-r-makes-the-case-for-meeting-your-heroes/) debuted in the U.S., and Acura is commemorating the anniversary with a callback car: the 2027 Integra Type S Heritage Edition. Only 700 units will be allocated for North America, and those Heritage Edition models will be the only way to get a 2027 Integra in Blazing Phoenix Yellow. The new color was inspired by Phoenix Yellow, last seen on the 2001 Integra. The bright hue will be paired with 10-spoke, 19×9.5-inch alloy copper-finish wheels and the Ebony interior accented with yellow stitching on the seats, steering wheel, door panels, center console, and shifter boot.


The Ebony interior that’s paired with the Heritage Edition is also available on the standard Integra Type S.


Acura


The Heritage Edition will feature an exclusive titanium shift knob as another nod to the Japanese-market DC2 Integra Type R.


Acura


“The original Integra Type R became an icon because it delivered an exhilarating yet attainable, and unmistakably Acura performance experience, and the Acura Integra Type S Heritage Edition is an incredible way to honor that legacy,” said Mamadou Diallo, executive vice president of the Auto Business Center at American Honda Motor Co., Inc. “For 2027, we’re taking the Integra Type S even further with refreshed styling and more standard features, enhancing the experience of driving the most powerful, best-performing Integra ever.”


Acura


Acura


The upgrades aren’t limited to the Heritage Edition, however. Other enhancements to the 2027 Integra Type S include new gloss black mirror caps and yellow Brembo brake calipers. All Type S models will benefit from new interior designs with dark gray interior trim. And the yellow-accented Ebony interior used in the Heritage Edition is just one option. There’s also a redesigned Orchid upholstery with blue accents, and an updated Red interior option with black accents. All Integra Type S models will also get a standard driver memory seat, driver/passenger mirror reverse tilt down, and memory brake hold for 2027.


Acura


Acura


Acura


Our very own managing editor, Eddy Eckart, has plenty of Type S experience. “As an owner of a Type S, I love the callback, and wish the color had been available when I bought mine almost three years ago. The Type R and Type S are dynamically very different cars, but the through-line as the most engaging, smile-inducing front-wheel-drive cars of their eras is worth celebrating,” said Eckart. “The incremental improvements Acura’s made for ’27 are a bonus—little things like a memory driver’s seat and tilt-down mirrors should be expected for $56K. Next wish: More sound deadening. I’ll take 20 more pounds of curb weight to be able to hear the excellent stereo a little better.”


All Integra Type S models remain powered by a 320-hp, turbocharged 2.0-liter VTEC engine that comes standard with a six-speed manual transaxle with automatic rev-matching and a limited-slip differential. The 2027 Acura Integra Type S will have a starting MSRP of $55,995, while the Type S Heritage Edition will start at $58,295. They’ll begin arriving at dealerships in December.
